environment: pinned Node 22.23.1 and Chromium via Playwright; actual modules, fake localStorage, mocked Fetch, inert loopback build; no network, account, credential, QR device or live service

red_before_fix.assertion: stale QR exchange must not overwrite a later session
red_before_fix.limitation: Actual service module with mocked Fetch and a simulated later session; not a browser journey or live exploit.

tests: a delayed QR exchange cannot overwrite a later session
a delayed anonymous bootstrap cannot publish after logout and a later login
cancelling an attempt prevents a held exchange from publishing
a rejected exchange redacts the code and nonce and keeps the anonymous session
a malformed exchange response is rejected without publishing
a current valid exchange establishes the account through the common path
a delayed AuthManager TV exchange cannot publish over a later session
a delayed email sign-in cannot publish over a later session
the QR image URL policy accepts only local, same-origin or image-data destinations

green_after_fix.result: exit 0; staleExchangeAccepted false, laterSessionOverwritten false, requests 1
green_after_fix.assertion: stale QR exchange must not overwrite a later session

tests: the actual QR screen completes a synthetic current flow with a safe local image
a hostile QR image URL renders as inert unavailable state and is never requested
leaving the screen during a held exchange has no later token or navigation side effect

ownership_changes: QrLoginService.beginAttempt/cancelAttempt define an explicit attempt with the current AuthManager session generation. start/poll/exchange accept the attempt id and check ownership after every awaited boundary.
A superseded or cancelled exchange cannot write tokens, mark an anonymous session authenticated, call get_sync_owner or navigate; the screen's post-await check is no longer the only protection.

Successful exchange publishes through AuthManager.establishAuthenticatedSession with a new authentication attempt. AuthManager increments an authentication-attempt sequence on sign-in, TV exchange, bootstrap and sign-out so stale email/TV/bootstrap completions cannot overwrite a later session.
Cleanup invalidates the attempt and clears an unapproved anonymous caller's tokens. Already-issued remote requests cannot be undone; the local publication boundary is what is controlled.
QR error text is redacted for the code and device nonce; console diagnostics use fixed messages.
rendering_changes: Removed the external api.qrserver.com image fallback; start() returns only an upstream qr_image_url or null.
isSafeQrImageUrl accepts same-origin HTTPS, the fixture loopback HTTP origin, or base64 image data; rejects javascript:, cross-origin, credential-bearing and quote/control-character URLs.
The screen creates the image node with document.createElement, sets src/alt as properties and uses textContent for the explicit unavailable state.
Hostile image URL test asserts no image node, no script execution, no evil-host request and zero external QR renderer requests.
browser_test_limits: Synthetic identity/add-on origins only; no live Nuvio service, QR consent or device observation.
The safe-image test uses the bundled logo as a same-origin stand-in, not a scannable QR code.
The held-exchange test proves no later local token/state/navigation side effect; it does not prove the upstream exchange was not processed server-side.
residual_risks: Tokens remain in same-origin localStorage; a same-origin script can still read them. This change does not eliminate that architecture or claim the application is XSS-proof.
Local sign-out/cleanup is not proof of remote session revocation.
Live QR approval, consent, expiry, nonce and device behavior remain blocked under #120 and are not claimed here.
review: Separate automated technical review recorded in docs/agent-runs/2026-10-20-issue7-ch2-review.md; not independent human approval.
